title: Throughput fidelity validator and customer-facing acceptance scenarios
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver a repeatable, high-fidelity throughput validation harness and a set of customer-facing acceptance scenarios that prove Redwood Dedicated capacity meets documented throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies.

Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect not just peak numbers but predictable sustained throughput at tail-latency SLOs under realistic traffic shapes. Existing tooling exercises raw throughput but does not capture real-world concerns: cache warmup characteristics, KV cache priming, continuous batching effects, model kernel selection shifts across sequence length distributions, cross-tenant interference, and autoscaler convergence during bursts and gradual ramps. This ticket consolidates learnings into a single validator suite that can produce: (1) benchmarking reports for internal certification, (2) deterministic acceptance test packs for customers, and (3) a small harness that customers (or Solutions Engineering) can run to validate their reservation.

Scope:
- Build a modular load harness that can simulate realistic traffic shapes (spikes, back-to-back short queries, long-padding sequences, mixed embed/gen workloads).
- Implement priming workflows (KV/prefix seeds) and warmup automation so throughput numbers reflect steady-state behaviour customers will see.
- Measure and report per-model and per-route metrics including p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, 99.9 tail, sustained tokens/sec, batching efficiency, and token-cost delta with/without quantization profiles.
- Add autoscaling policy verification: ensure configured scaling curves meet target latency/throughput under controlled burst and degradation scenarios; surface time-to-scale and overshoot.
- Produce documented customer acceptance scripts and a condensed report template (so Solutions or Customer SRE can validate a Dedicated reservation).
acceptance_criteria: Modular harness repo and CI job that can run a standard benchmark against a dedicated pool and produce machine-readable reports (JSON+CSV)
Benchmarks include KV cache priming, steady-state measurement after warmup, and at least three traffic shapes (ramp, spike, sustained mixed) with p99 latency assertions
Autoscaling verification scenarios that validate scale-up/scale-down times within configured thresholds and detect oscillations or overshoot
Customer acceptance pack (scripted steps + report template) with clear pass/fail rules and a runbook for Solutions Engineering
test_plan: Design traffic shape library: define parameterizable ramp, spike, and mixed workloads (requests/sec, sequence length distribution, concurrency)
Implement harness modules: generator, priming module (KV/prefix), metric collector (Prometheus + direct runtime hooks), result aggregator
Create warmup orchestration: automated priming, cache stabilization window, and steady-state start signal
Run baseline benchmarks against staging dedicated pools and compare against historical throughput cert numbers
Run autoscaler stress tests: controlled burst to 5x baseline, hold, and observe time-to-first-scale and time-to-stable; run gradual ramp to verify slope behavior
Validate harness across model variants (float32, int8-q, quantized kernels) and GPU types; record kernel-selection shifts
Package customer acceptance scripts and produce example reports for two sample customers (SaaS analytics and regulated finance)
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Scoping complete; defined three canonical traffic shapes and required metrics. Prototype harness design approved by runtime team.
2026-03-03: Initial generator and priming module implemented; validated priming reduces p99 by ~18% in local run. Shared prototype with Solutions Engineering for feedback.
2026-03-10: Ran baseline against staging dedicated pool. Observed kernel selection change at sequence length >1024 causing throughput drop; added sequence-slicing config to harness.
2026-03-14: Autoscaler stress tests added. Observed scale-up latency for burst test ~45s (target <30s) — opened follow-up ENG-20173 for autoscaler tuning.
notes: Trade-offs: Full fidelity harness requires access to runtime hooks (kernel metrics) that expose implementation details. For customer-facing acceptance pack we will provide a restricted mode that relies on black-box Prometheus metrics.

Risk: Running high-fidelity tests on production-dedicated pools can be disruptive; recommend dedicated staging pools for certification runs and a lightweight smoke acceptance for on-customer-run verification.
Future: Consider adding RL-based traffic synthesizer to better model customer-specific token distributions (out of scope for this ticket).
customer_test_scripts: script-01-prime-and-warmup.sh - executes KV/prefix priming and marks steady-state start
script-02-sustained-throughput.yml - runs mixed gen/embed workload for 30 minutes and captures p99/p95
script-03-burst-autoscale-check.sh - triggers 5x burst and records scale events and time-to-stabilize
